Two independent address bounds now exist and NOTHING asserts their relationship. NVGspStage.hpp enforces a POLICY ceiling of NV_GSP_FW_ADDR_BITS = 41 bits (NV_GSP_FW_PHYS_LIMIT). NVGspBoot.hpp now enforces a REPRESENTABILITY bound of 17 bits of physAddrHi (NVGSP_DMA_PHYSHI_MASK, derived from DMATRFBASE1_BASE_MASK), which is physical bits 48:32 -- i.e. 49 bits total. The invariant that makes the pair safe is POLICY <= REPRESENTABLE: the stage header must never admit an address the boot header would truncate. Nothing checks that today, and the two headers cannot reference each other (NVGspStage.hpp includes NVGspBoot.hpp, not the reverse), so a future widening of NV_GSP_FW_ADDR_BITS past 49 would compile clean and silently reintroduce truncation. Add an assertion of POLICY <= REPRESENTABLE. Put it where BOTH constants are visible -- test_gsp_stage.cpp includes NVGspStage.hpp which pulls in NVGspBoot.hpp, so it can see both; check-registers.py is the alternative if a host-side static check is preferred. Assert with SEPARATING inputs: the highest address the policy admits must satisfy nvGspDmaPhysHiFits() on its high word, and a hand-computed address one bit above the representability bound must fail it. Do NOT write 41, 17 or 49 as literals -- derive every one from the existing constants, or the assertion goes stale exactly when the definition it guards is edited.
